question: A man walks to a viewpoint and returns to the starting point by his car maintaining constant speed and thus takes a total time of 5 hours 30 minutes. He would have gained 3 hours by driving both ways. How long would it have taken for him to walk both ways with same walking speed?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let W be the time to walk one way and D be the time to drive one way.

Given: W + D = 5 hours 30 minutes.

Since replacing one walk with a drive saves 3 hours, conversely, replacing one drive with a walk will add 3 hours.

⇒ Time to walk both ways (2W) = (W + D) + 3 hours.

⇒ 2W = 5 hours 30 minutes + 3 hours = 8 hours 30 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 hours 30 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken to walk one way and drive back (W + D) = 5 hours 30 minutes = 5.5 hours.

Time gained by driving both ways instead of mixed travel = 3 hours.

 
•

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time to drive both ways (2D) = 5.5 − 3 = 2.5 hours.

⇒ Time to drive one way (D) = 2.5 ÷ 2 = 1.25 hours = 1 hour 15 minutes.

⇒ Time to walk one way (W) = 5.5 − 1.25 = 4.25 hours = 4 hours 15 minutes.

⇒ Time to walk both ways (2W) = 2 × 4.25 = 8.5 hours.

⇒ 8.5 hours = 8 hours 30 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 hours 30 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Constant Distance)

When a person travels a distance at speed S₁ and returns at speed S₂, the average speed for the whole journey is (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Relation between Speed and Time

When the distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to the time taken. If the ratio of speeds is a : b, the respective ratio of time taken will be b : a.

Relative Speed Concept

When two moving bodies travel in the same direction, their relative speed is calculated as the difference of their speeds. When moving in opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds.
